Hi Samir — Monica here (implementation lead). Answers inline below.

1) Cutover window: 2026-11-12 02:00-04:00 UTC is acceptable from our side. We recommend a 30-minute canary at 10% traffic, then 1 hour at 50% before full shift.

2) Retries/Idempotency: For write operations we strongly recommend client-supplied idempotency keys (Idempotency-Key header). Our servers honor the header for 24 hours and provide a 409 conflict when duplicate non-idempotent requests are received. For transient transport errors (timeouts, 502/503) use exponential backoff with jitter and retry up to 4 attempts.

Example cURL (simple):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/infer \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RDW_KEY" \n  -H "Idempotency-Key: <uuid>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

Recommended client defaults (SDK):
- connectTimeoutMs: 5_000
- timeoutMs (overall): 60_000
- maxRetries: 4 (only for retryable HTTP 429, 502, 503, 504, network errors)
- backoffBaseMs: 250, factor: 2, jitter: true
- per-route token bucket: 200 requests/min default (adjust per-account)

Rate-limit headers we return (and that your gateway can surface):
- X-RDW-RateLimit-Limit: overall allowed QPS/min
- X-RDW-RateLimit-Remaining: remaining in current window
- X-RDW-RateLimit-Reset: epoch seconds when window resets

Attachments: I'll add SDK samples (sdk-snippets.tar.gz) that include:
- Node/Go/python examples for exponential backoff and idempotency handling
- A small harness for smoke testing the new endpoint (local-run.sh)
- A checklist for cutover rollback triggers (error-rate > 5% over 5min, median latency > 2s)

Endpoint migration steps (short):
- Point sandbox key at new endpoint, run smoke tests (3k requests)
- Enable telemetry & quota guard in prod for new key (observability baseline)
- Canary 10% for 30 minutes (monitor errors/latency)
- If stable, ramp to 50% for 1 hour then to 100%
- Keep old route available for 48 hours for emergency rollback

I'll be on the kickoff to walk through the SDK bits.

Thanks,
